text:
COP gained 0.84% today, recovering from a sharp drop on November 18th when the stock fell nearly $5 (3.7%). The bounce follows a modest uptick in U.S. oil prices to $89.53 per barrel, though this remains well below the $142+ levels from earlier this month. The rebound also comes as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East resurface—Saudi Arabia and Bahrain reported new attacks linked to Iran and Iranian-backed forces—which historically can support oil prices by raising concerns about supply disruption, even if prices haven't spiked dramatically in response yet.

The broader energy backdrop remains supportive for oil companies: Europe is facing tight gas markets due to low storage and cold weather, data centers are driving a structural increase in electricity demand, and the Senate passed permitting reform that could accelerate energy infrastructure projects. These trends underpin long-term demand for oil and gas, though near-term sentiment appears cautious given the two-week chart showing COP essentially flat despite the recent volatility.
